planting.note: Direct sow in loose, stone-free soil as soon as it can be worked, keeping the bed evenly moist until seedlings emerge since carrot seed germinates slowly.

directions: Touchon is a classic French heirloom carrot of the Nantes type, prized for smooth, nearly coreless, cylindrical roots with a blunt tip and exceptionally sweet, crisp flesh. Direct sow seed thinly and shallowly in deeply worked, stone-free soil, then thin seedlings to about 2 inches apart once true leaves appear to give roots room to size up straight and uniform. It tolerates light frost well and holds good eating quality in the ground longer than many thin-skinned Nantes types, making it useful for a succession of plantings from early spring into fall. Harvest at finger size for the sweetest, most tender roots, or let them reach full size for storage.

planting.note: Direct sow early in cool soil; this short-rooted, fast-maturing type suits shallow or heavy soils where longer carrots struggle to form straight roots.

directions: Early Scarlet Horn is one of the oldest named carrot varieties still in circulation, a short, blunt, horn-shaped root tracing back to early French market gardens long before the longer Nantes and Imperator types were developed. Direct sow seed shallowly in cool soil in early spring, thinning seedlings to about 2 inches apart; the stubby 4 to 5 inch roots mature quickly and tolerate the shallow or stony soils that defeat longer-rooted carrots. Its small size and rapid maturity made it historically valuable for early spring crops and for forcing under frames before the ground fully warmed. Pull roots as soon as they reach usable size, since quality declines and roots can become woody if left too long in warm soil.

planting.note: Direct sow into deeply dug, loose soil so the long tapering root can develop straight; a long season crop best started once soil has warmed slightly.

directions: Altrincham is an old English carrot named for the Cheshire market town where it was traditionally grown, producing a long, tapering orange root with a distinctive green-tinged shoulder above ground. Work the bed deeply before sowing so the root can push straight down without forking, and thin seedlings to several inches apart once established. It is a long-season type best suited to a full spring-to-fall growing window, rewarding patience with dense, sweet flesh that stores well after a fall harvest. Lift roots before hard freezes and trim the tops for winter storage in a cool, humid root cellar.

planting.note: Sow in late summer or early fall for overwintering under light cover; this old hardy type is bred to survive cold rather than for quick spring growth.

directions: Arctic King is an old hardy cabbage-type lettuce bred specifically to survive winter in the open garden or under minimal frame protection, standing through hard frosts that would collapse most other lettuces. Sow in late summer or early fall so plants reach a small, firm rosette before the coldest weather sets in, then let growth resume slowly as days lengthen for an early spring harvest. The compact, pale green heads fold into a dense, blanched heart that stays sweet rather than bitter through cold spells. Where winters are too harsh for open-ground survival, a cold frame or row cover substantially improves the odds of carrying plants through to spring.
